senses.def: to make something firmer, tighter, or more secure, or to become so
examples: Use a wrench to tighten the bolts on the wheel.
His grip tightened on the steering wheel.

senses.def: to make rules, controls, or laws stricter
examples: After the attack, the airport tightened security.
The government plans to tighten rules on gun sales.

note: Opposite: loosen. "Tighten your belt" = spend less money (kemerleri sıkmak).

senses.def: up to a particular time; until
examples: The store is open till nine on weekdays.
I'll be at the office till late tonight.

senses.def: up to the point when something happens; until
examples: Wait here till I come back.
We didn't leave till the rain stopped.

note: Informal; "until" is preferred in formal writing. Not a short form of "until", so don't write "'til" in formal texts.

senses.def: trees grown to be used for building or making things, or wood prepared for this
examples: The region's economy depends on timber and fishing.
Illegal timber harvesting is destroying the rainforest.

senses.def: a large piece of wood used in building a house or ship
examples: The old barn was held up by huge oak timbers.

note: Americans usually call cut wood for building "lumber"; "timber" is more British for this sense.

senses.def: what is measured in minutes, hours, days, etc., or the amount available to do something
examples: I don't have time to cook tonight.
Time goes by so fast when you're on vacation.

senses.def: a particular point in the day, shown on a clock
examples: What time does the movie start?
Excuse me, do you have the time?

senses.def: an occasion when something happens
examples: This is the third time I've lost my keys this month.
Next time, call before you come.

senses.def: to plan when something happens, or to measure how long something takes
examples: The protest was timed to coincide with the president's visit.
Time yourself to see how fast you can run a mile.

note: "On time" = at the planned time (tam vaktinde); "in time" = early enough (zamanında, geç kalmadan).

senses.def: happening at exactly the right time or soon enough to be useful
examples: Thanks to the timely arrival of the firefighters, no one was hurt.
The report is a timely reminder of the dangers of drunk driving.

note: An adjective, not an adverb. Say "in a timely manner", not "timely" alone after a verb. "Untimely death" = early death.

senses.def: the choice of when something happens, or the time when it happens
examples: The timing of the announcement surprised investors.
Good timing! I was just about to call you.

senses.def: the skill of doing something at exactly the right moment
examples: A good comedian needs perfect timing.

senses.def: a metal container with a lid for storing or selling food
examples: Grandma kept her cookies in an old tin on the kitchen shelf.
Open a tin of tomatoes and add them to the pan.

senses.def: a soft, silver-white metal often used to cover other metals
examples: The old cabin had a tin roof that was loud in the rain.

note: For canned food, Americans say "can" (a can of beans); "tin" is British. Americans use "tin" for cookie or baking containers.

senses.def: extremely small in size or amount
examples: They live in a tiny apartment in downtown Boston.
Only a tiny fraction of the money reached the victims.

note: Comparatives: tinier, tiniest. Opposite: huge, enormous.

senses.def: a small piece of practical advice
examples: The article gives some useful tips for saving money on groceries.
Here's a tip: book your flights on a Tuesday.

senses.def: extra money given to a waiter, driver, etc. to thank them for their service
examples: In the US, people usually leave a tip of 15 to 20 percent.

senses.def: the thin pointed end of something
examples: He burned the tip of his finger on the stove.

senses.def: to give someone extra money for their service
examples: Did you tip the taxi driver?

collocations: on the tip of my tongue
note: "On the tip of my tongue" = dilimin ucunda. "Tip of the iceberg" = buzdağının görünen kısmı. "Tip over" = devirmek/devrilmek.

senses.def: a thick rubber ring that fits around the wheel of a car, bicycle, etc.
examples: We got a flat tire on the way to the airport.
Check your tire pressure before a long drive.

senses.def: to become tired, or to lose interest in something
examples: My grandmother tires easily these days.
He never tires of telling the same old stories.

note: American spelling "tire"; British spelling for the wheel is "tyre".

senses.def: feeling that you need to rest or sleep
examples: I was so tired after the flight that I slept for twelve hours.
You look tired. Did you sleep badly?

senses.def: bored or annoyed with something because it has continued too long
examples: I'm tired of hearing the same excuses every week.

note: "Tired" = how you feel; "tiring" = what causes it: "a tiring day made me tired". "Tired of" = bored with (-den bıkmak).

senses.def: a piece of soft, thin paper used especially for blowing your nose
examples: Can you pass me a tissue? I think I'm getting a cold.
She kept a box of tissues on her desk.

senses.def: the material that animals and plants are made of, consisting of cells
examples: The doctor removed a small sample of tissue for testing.
Scar tissue formed over the wound.

note: Americans often call a paper tissue a "Kleenex", a brand name used generically.

senses.def: the name of a book, film, song, painting, etc.
examples: What's the title of the book you're reading?
The album's title track became a hit.

senses.def: a word like Dr., Mrs., or Professor used before a name, or a name describing someone's job
examples: Her official job title is Senior Data Analyst.

senses.def: the position of being the winner of a sports competition
examples: The team won its third straight league title.

senses.def: to give a book, song, etc. a particular name
examples: Her first novel was titled "The Long Way Home."

senses.def: in the direction of a place, person, or thing
examples: We're driving to Florida next week.
Give the letter to your teacher.

senses.def: used to show the end of a range or period, or the minutes before an hour
examples: The museum is open from nine to five.
It's ten to six, so we should leave soon.

senses.def: used before the base form of a verb, often to show purpose
examples: I want to learn to play the guitar.
She went to the bank to get some cash.

note: Turkish speakers often add "for" before purpose: say "I came to help", not "I came for to help" or "for help me".

senses.def: the dried leaves of a plant that are smoked in cigarettes, pipes, etc.
examples: Many states have raised taxes on tobacco products.
The farm has grown tobacco for three generations.

note: Uncountable: "tobacco", not "a tobacco". "Tobacco use" covers smoking and chewing.

senses.def: on this day
examples: I have three meetings today.
Is the pharmacy open today?

senses.def: at the present time, in this period of history
examples: Today, most people get their news from their phones.

senses.def: this day, or the present period of time
examples: Today is my parents' anniversary.
Today's teenagers face very different pressures.

note: No preposition before it: "I'll do it today", not "in today".

senses.def: one of the five small parts at the end of the foot
examples: I stubbed my toe on the coffee table.
She stood on her toes to reach the top shelf.

note: English separates finger (el parmağı) and toe (ayak parmağı). "Step on someone's toes" = offend them by interfering.

senses.def: with or near each other
examples: We've worked together for over ten years.
Let's go to the game together.

senses.def: so that two or more things are joined, mixed, or combined
examples: Mix the butter and sugar together until smooth.
Taken together, the results suggest the drug works.

note: "Get your act together" (informal) = start organizing your life better.

senses.def: a large bowl connected to a pipe, used for getting rid of waste from the body
examples: Don't forget to flush the toilet.
The toilet in the downstairs bathroom keeps running.

note: In the US, the room is usually called "the bathroom" (at home) or "the restroom" (in public); "toilet" usually means the bowl itself.

senses.def: willingness to accept opinions, beliefs, or behavior that you don't agree with
examples: The school promotes tolerance and respect for all religions.
He has little tolerance for laziness.

senses.def: the ability to bear pain, hardship, or a substance without being harmed
examples: Over time, the body builds up a tolerance to caffeine.
Some plants have a high tolerance for drought.

note: "Zero tolerance" = a policy of punishing every case, with no exceptions.

senses.tr: hoş görmek, göz yummak, izin vermek
senses.def: to allow something you don't like or agree with to exist or happen
examples: The manager said he would not tolerate rudeness to customers.
Bullying will not be tolerated at this school.

senses.def: to be able to bear something unpleasant, or to take a drug without harm
examples: I can't tolerate the heat in Arizona in July.
Most patients tolerate the medication well.

senses.def: money you pay to use a particular road, bridge, or tunnel
examples: The toll on the bridge went up to eight dollars.
We took a toll road to avoid traffic.

senses.def: the number of people killed or injured in a disaster, war, etc.
examples: The death toll from the earthquake has risen to over two hundred.

senses.def: the harm or damage caused by something over time
examples: Years of night shifts took a heavy toll on his health.

note: "Take a toll on" = cause damage over time. A "toll-free number" is a free phone number (ücretsiz hat).

senses.def: a soft, round, red fruit with a lot of juice, eaten raw or cooked as a vegetable
examples: Slice a few tomatoes for the salad.
This pasta sauce is made with fresh tomatoes and basil.

note: Plural: tomatoes. American pronunciation /təˈmeɪtoʊ/ ("to-MAY-to"); British /təˈmɑːtəʊ/.

senses.def: on the day after today
examples: I'll call you tomorrow after work.
The package should arrive tomorrow morning.

senses.def: the day after today, or the future
examples: Tomorrow is a holiday, so the banks are closed.
We're training the leaders of tomorrow.

note: "The day after tomorrow" = öbür gün. No preposition: "tomorrow morning", not "in tomorrow morning".

senses.def: a unit of weight; in the US, 2,000 pounds (about 907 kg)
examples: The truck was carrying ten tons of steel.
The bridge can hold vehicles up to forty tons.

senses.def: (informal) a very large amount or number
examples: I've got tons of homework this weekend.
This bag weighs a ton!

collocations: hit like a ton of bricks
note: A US ton = 2,000 lb; a metric ton (tonne) = 1,000 kg. "Tons of" is very common informally for "a lot of".

senses.def: the quality of someone's voice that shows their feelings or attitude
examples: Don't use that tone of voice with me.
She spoke in a calm, friendly tone.

senses.def: the general mood or character of something, such as a piece of writing or an event
examples: The opening speech set a positive tone for the conference.
The tone of the email was a little too formal.

senses.def: a shade of a color, or a single sound made by an electronic device
examples: The walls are painted in warm earth tones.
Leave a message after the tone.

note: "Tone down" = make less extreme or offensive. "Toned" body = firm, muscular.

senses.def: the soft, moving part in your mouth used for tasting, swallowing, and speaking
examples: I burned my tongue on the hot coffee.
The doctor asked him to stick out his tongue.

senses.def: (formal) a language
examples: Her mother tongue is Turkish, but she writes in English.

collocations: on the tip of my tongue
note: Pronounced /tʌŋ/, rhymes with "young". "Tongue-in-cheek" = said as a joke, not seriously.

senses.def: on the evening or night of today
examples: What are you doing tonight?
The game starts at eight tonight.

senses.def: the evening or night of today
examples: Tonight's dinner is on me.

note: Turkish "bu akşam" is usually "tonight" or "this evening"; "last night" (not "yesterday night") = dün gece.

senses.def: a metric unit of weight equal to 1,000 kilograms
examples: The factory produces about 500 tonnes of steel a day.
The country exported two million tonnes of wheat last year.

note: British spelling. Americans usually say "metric ton" for 1,000 kg; a US "ton" is 2,000 pounds.

senses.def: more than is good, necessary, or possible
examples: This coffee is too hot to drink.
You're driving too fast; slow down.

senses.def: also; as well
examples: I'd like a coffee too, please.
She speaks Spanish, and Italian too.

note: "Too" is negative (more than needed): "too expensive" ≠ "very expensive". Use "either" in negatives: "I don't either."

senses.def: an instrument such as a hammer or saw that you hold and use for making or repairing things
examples: He keeps his tools in a box in the garage.
You'll need a special tool to remove the screws.

senses.def: something that helps you do a particular job or achieve something
examples: Social media is a powerful tool for small businesses.
The app is a useful tool for learning vocabulary.

senses.def: one of the hard white objects in the mouth used for biting and chewing
examples: I chipped a tooth on a popcorn kernel and had to see a dentist.
Brush your teeth before bed.

note: Irregular plural: teeth. "Have a sweet tooth" = love sweet foods (tatlı düşkünü olmak).

senses.def: the highest part or point of something, or a cover or lid
examples: We climbed to the top of the hill to watch the sunset.
Put the top back on the bottle.

senses.tr: en üst, en yüksek; en iyi
senses.def: highest in position, rank, or quality
examples: The files are in the top drawer.
She's one of the top lawyers in the city.

senses.def: a piece of clothing worn on the upper body
examples: She wore a black top and jeans.

senses.def: to be higher than a particular amount, or to be first in a list
examples: Sales topped $2 billion last year.
The song topped the charts for six weeks.

note: "On top of that" = besides, in addition (üstelik). "Top up" (British) = refill.

senses.def: a subject that people talk, write, or learn about
examples: Climate change was the main topic of the debate.
Let's change the topic; this is getting too serious.

note: "Topical" = relating to current events (güncel).

senses.def: the act of causing someone severe pain to punish them or make them give information
examples: The prisoners described years of torture and abuse.
International law bans the use of torture.

senses.def: great mental or physical suffering, or something very unpleasant
examples: Sitting through that three-hour meeting was pure torture.

senses.def: to cause someone severe physical or mental pain
examples: The regime tortured political prisoners.
He was tortured by guilt for years after the accident.

senses.def: to throw something lightly or carelessly
examples: She tossed her keys onto the table.
Toss me that towel, would you?

senses.def: to throw a coin into the air to make a decision by chance
examples: Let's toss a coin to see who goes first.

senses.def: to mix food lightly so it is covered with a sauce or dressing
examples: Toss the pasta with olive oil and garlic.

note: "Toss and turn" = move around in bed because you can't sleep. "It's a toss-up" = both outcomes are equally likely.

senses.def: being the full amount after everything is added together
examples: The total cost of the trip was about $3,000.
The company has a total of 400 employees.

senses.def: complete; used for emphasis
examples: The party was a total disaster.
He's a total stranger to me.

senses.def: the amount you get when you add several numbers together
examples: Add up the numbers and write the total at the bottom.
In total, we raised over $10,000 for the shelter.

senses.def: to reach a particular amount when added up
examples: Damages from the storm totaled more than $5 million.

note: American spelling: totaled, totaling; British: totalled, totalling. "Total a car" (informal) = destroy it completely.

senses.def: completely
examples: I totally forgot about the meeting.
The two cases are totally different.

senses.def: (informal) used to strongly agree with someone
examples: "That movie was amazing." "Totally!"

senses.def: to put your hand or another part of your body on someone or something
examples: Please don't touch the paintings.
She touched his arm gently to get his attention.

senses.def: to make someone feel emotion, especially sympathy or gratitude
examples: We were deeply touched by your kind letter.

senses.def: the act of touching, or the sense that lets you feel things with your skin
examples: The fabric is soft to the touch.
The screen responds to the lightest touch.

senses.def: communication with someone
examples: We still keep in touch after twenty years.
I'll be in touch next week.

note: "Keep in touch" = stay in contact (görüşmeye devam etmek). "Touch on a subject" = mention it briefly.

senses.def: difficult, with a lot of problems
examples: It's been a tough year for the restaurant industry.
We had to make some tough decisions about the budget.

senses.def: strong enough to deal with difficult conditions or rough treatment
examples: You have to be tough to survive in this business.
These boots are made of tough leather.

senses.def: strict and determined
examples: The mayor promised to get tough on crime.

note: Pronounced /tʌf/ like "stuff". "Tough meat" = hard to chew. "Tough luck!" = too bad (often unsympathetic).

senses.def: a trip for pleasure in which several places are visited, or a short visit around a building
examples: We took a guided tour of the White House.
They went on a two-week tour of Italy.

senses.def: a series of performances or games in different places
examples: The band is on tour in Europe this summer.

senses.def: to travel around a place, or to perform in different places
examples: We toured the vineyards of Napa Valley.
The orchestra is touring Asia next year.

senses.def: the business of providing hotels, services, and entertainment for people traveling for pleasure
examples: Tourism is the island's main source of income.
The pandemic hit the tourism industry hard.

senses.def: a person who is traveling or visiting a place for pleasure
examples: The museum is full of tourists in the summer.
Venice attracts millions of tourists every year.

note: "Tourist trap" = a place that overcharges tourists. "Touristy" (informal) is often negative.

senses.def: a sports competition in which players or teams who lose are eliminated until one winner is left
examples: Our team made it to the semifinals of the tournament.
She won her first tennis tournament at fifteen.

note: "Turnuva" maps directly to "tournament"; "league" is a season-long competition.

senses.def: in the direction of someone or something
examples: The dog came running towards me.
She walked towards the exit without looking back.

senses.def: in relation to someone or something
examples: His attitude towards work has changed a lot.

senses.def: as a contribution to paying for or achieving something
examples: We're saving towards a down payment on a house.
This is an important step towards peace.

note: "Toward" (no -s) is standard in American English; "towards" is mainly British.

senses.def: a piece of cloth or paper used for drying your body or things
examples: Grab a towel from the closet before you get in the pool.
Wipe up the spill with a paper towel.

note: "Throw in the towel" = give up, admit defeat (pes etmek).

senses.def: a tall, narrow building or part of a building, such as a church or castle
examples: The clock tower in the town square was built in 1890.
We climbed the tower for a view of the city.

senses.def: a tall building or structure used for a particular purpose
examples: They live on the 30th floor of an office tower downtown.
The cell tower was damaged in the storm.

note: As a verb, "tower over" = be much taller than: "He towers over his classmates."

senses.def: a place with many houses and businesses, larger than a village but smaller than a city
examples: She grew up in a small town in Ohio.
The whole town came out for the parade.

senses.def: the central area of a town where the shops and businesses are
examples: I'm going into town to do some shopping.

note: "Out of town" = away from where you live (şehir dışında). "In town" = currently here.

senses.def: containing poison, or harmful to people, animals, or the environment
examples: The factory was fined for dumping toxic waste into the river.
Some household cleaners are toxic if swallowed.

senses.def: very unpleasant and harmful to people's well-being
examples: She left the company because of its toxic work culture.
It took him years to get out of a toxic relationship.

senses.def: an object for children to play with
examples: The kids left their toys all over the living room floor.
He got a remote-control car for his birthday and it's his favorite toy.

senses.def: made as a small copy of something, for playing with
examples: My son loves playing with his toy trains.

note: As a verb, "toy with an idea" = consider it, but not seriously (aklından geçirmek).
